gaps.sentence: We must take ___ for our own health (RESPONSIBLE).
gaps.explanation: 'Take responsibility for something' is the fixed phrase; the -ity noun is needed.

gaps.sentence: Their ___ goes back to their schooldays (FRIEND).
gaps.hint: noun needed: the state of being friends (-ship)
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ship forms nouns of state: friendship means the relationship between friends.

gaps.sentence: The ___ (PROSPER) of the region depends on tourism.
The ___ of the new bridge will take two years (CONSTRUCT).
gaps.hint: noun needed as subject of the sentence
gaps.explanation: The subject needs a noun: construction (the -tion noun); 'constructive' is an adjective.

gaps.sentence: He lost his job because of his ___ (HONESTY).
gaps.hint: negative noun needed — he lost his job
gaps.explanation: Losing a job implies wrongdoing, so the negative noun 'dishonesty' (dis- + honesty) is needed.

gaps.hint: noun needed after 'His'; note the -al suffix
gaps.explanation: The noun of 'refuse' is 'refusal' (-al noun); 'refuse' as a noun means rubbish.

gaps.sentence: New technology has ___ the way we work (REVOLUTION).
gaps.explanation: The suffix -ise forms the verb: revolutionise. After 'has' the past participle 'revolutionised' is needed.

gaps.hint: negative adjective needed (-ish): not appropriate for an adult
gaps.explanation: 'Childish' is negative (silly, immature); 'childlike' is positive (innocent). The embarrassment shows the negative sense.
